name: Retainer and mouthguard cleaning

lead: Cleaning retainers, sports mouthguards and night guards is a hygiene habit meant to prevent bacterial buildup and odour, so your breath and mouth stay fresh while you wear them.

Appliances worn in the mouth collect biofilm on their surfaces, and cleaning removes it. Reference sources describe bacteria and yeast building up on porous acrylic dentures, a related appliance, and porous plastic as especially able to hold microbes. No studies specific to retainers or mouthguards were found.

paras: Users rinse and brush the appliance after wearing, and use cleaning products on a regular schedule. Manufacturers and dentists give product-specific care guidance, and the routine sits alongside normal brushing.
No harms from cleaning are reported in the sources consulted. Product-specific instructions matter, since materials and cleaners vary.

angle.text: Cleaning retainers and mouthguards routinely cuts bacterial buildup on the appliance, leaving less odour and a fresher mouth. The idea follows from research on denture hygiene; studies on retainers themselves were not found.

lead: Retainer and mouthguard cleaning refers to routine hygiene for removable oral appliances such as orthodontic retainers, sports mouthguards and night guards. In grooming-oriented communities it is mentioned as a way to avoid bacterial buildup and odour.

Reference material on closely related appliances notes that porous acrylic dentures can harbour bacteria and yeast and cause odour when not cleaned well [1]. Wikipedia's mouthguard article describes how occlusal splints are typically made of heat-cured acrylic or softer materials but does not discuss cleaning [2].
No studies specific to retainer or mouthguard cleaning were identified for this article, so the entry is short.

paras: The practice involves regularly cleaning removable appliances that sit in the mouth. Cleaning methods recommended by manufacturers and dentists vary and are not summarised here.

The halitosis article identifies unclean acrylic dentures as an intra-oral source of odour because the plastic is porous and lets bacteria and yeast accumulate [1]. It does not address orthodontic retainers or mouthguards specifically [1].
The mouthguard article reports studies of low compliance with prescribed mouthguard use and describes materials and durability, without covering hygiene [2].
